1.5 Net Zero Key technological breakthroughs and rapid global policy coordination. OECD countries and China implement a transparent economy-wide carbon price mechanism by 2025 which rises from $50/tCO2e in 2030 to $200 by 2050. Other non-OECD nations follow by imposing economy-wide carbon prices of $10/tCO2e in 2030 rising to $50 by 2050. Global oil demand peaks in 2025 and declines to 50 MMBOD in 2050. The 1.5 Net Zero scenario is designed to reach net-zero emissions in the energy sector by 2050. The remaining carbon budget of 600 gigatonnes of cumulative CO2 emissions from 2020 to 2050 is in line with a 1.5-degree warming target before 2100 with a slight temperature overshoot around the middle of the century. See IPCC AR6 Synthesis Report (2023).

As a result of our strategy and scenario work, we have focused capital on resources with low cost of supply, exiting deep water and high emissions intensity gas fields while increasing our investments in unconventional oil projects. In recent years we have high-graded our portfolio and applied stringent capital allocation criteria that direct investments to resources that will best match future energy demand. We are equally focused on developing assets that have a low cost of supply and low GHG intensity, as these are most likely to compete in any future energy transition pathway with each asset type contributing to its unique market. Based on our current forecasts, assets with less than 10 kg CO2e/BOE are projected to represent a larger portion of our portfolio by 2030.

note: criteria 1, 3, 4 — 3 of 5. Criterion 1 satisfied by quantified IEA scenario oil prices (STEPS $81/NZE $43 per bbl in 2030; STEPS $77/NZE $26 in 2050), carbon price assumptions ($50/tCO2e rising to $200 in 2050 under 1.5 Net Zero), oil demand trajectory (50 MMBOD in 2050 under NZE), and 10 kg CO2e/BOE portfolio intensity projection by 2030 (Spans 1, 2, 3). Criterion 2 not satisfied: no named emissions reduction target with baseline and target year in selected spans. Criterion 3 satisfied by IPCC AR6 600 Gt carbon budget as calibration basis for the 1.5 Net Zero scenario (Span 2), cost-of-supply definition as 10% after-tax WTI-equivalent return (page 18), and the four-scenario global energy model. Criterion 4 satisfied by price projections to 2030, 2040, 2050 (Span 1) and explicit oil and gas demand peak years under NZE scenario (Span 2). Criterion 5 not satisfied per handbook rule: scenario projections are not historical multi-year metrics; trend_disclosed is never true for S3. scenario_linked = true: IEA STEPS (Stated Policies), APS (Announced Pledges), and NZE (Net Zero Emissions) all explicitly named in Span 1 (page 18) and on the handbook allowed list. uncertainty_discussed = true: scenario description section acknowledges wide-ranging assumption uncertainty (technological advances, government policies, consumer behavior); 1.5 Net Zero footnote acknowledges temperature overshoot uncertainty around the carbon budget. Boundary note: COP's four proprietary internal scenarios (Pre-Pandemic Trends, Moderate Transition, Accelerated Transition, 1.5 Net Zero on pages 13–14) are the primary scenario framework but do not satisfy scenario_linked because they are not on the allowed list; the IEA STEPS/APS/NZE table on page 18 provides the allowed-list evidence. Capital allocation responses in Span 3 (exiting deepwater, unconventional focus) also support S4 — cross-concept note.
